title: StitchVector automatic line extraction - minimal synthetic test (P1). Pushed and remote-verified before the test-seed run.
question: Without hand waypoints, can label-free code recover continuous, correctly placed lines on synthetic tiles with exact truth, while not drawing lines on 3-6 px fill-coloured bands?
scope: synthetic tiles only (sv_synth.py); no real sample, no sealed pool, no GIS product
targets_from_D71: anti-aliased red line with colour shading along the line must stay one connected ink region (no colour classes before line detection)
a red line starting inside a red fill must not be protected just because the fill is red

tile.content: pink background, green / yellow / red fill blobs; two fill-coloured bands 3-6 px; lines red_aa_2, red_aa_3 (shaded), black_1, black_3, black_5, pale_1, red_var_2to5 (width grows 2->5), red_touch_fill (starts inside the red fill)
tile.render: drawn at 4x with anti-aliasing, reduced with INTER_AREA, Gaussian noise sigma 2, JPEG q75

dev_disclosure: The detector (sv_autoline.py, params AL.P) was written and scored on dev seeds 1001-1003 before freeze (scored twice with identical deterministic output: once ad hoc, once via sv_autoline_run.py dev), with no parameter change after seeing the dev scores. One dev tile (1001) was viewed as an image; after that only the red_touch_fill note text in sv_synth.py was corrected and an unused helper removed. Dev results (in this commit as autoline_dev.json): most lines recall 0.74-1.0 but split into 3-7 objects; pale_1 recall 0.10-0.35; bands had a line on 2-6% of their axis. Test seeds 2001-2005 were never generated before freeze.
detector: sv_autoline.extract with AL.P (frozen in code): contrast vs 15x15 median (CIE76) -> fill colours from wide low-contrast regions -> protected = near a fill colour or on a fill/fill mixing segment -> ink = contrast > 12 and not protected -> skeleton chains -> spur removal -> straight-through joining at junctions (<= 35 deg) -> min length 10 px -> smooth + simplify 1 px. Width = median 2*EDT-1 on the skeleton.
baseline: D71 frozen L/P/U classifier (sv_d71.run_one on the 32-colour quantization of the same tile): recall of its L pixels along each truth line

per_line: recall: share of 1 px truth samples within 2 px of any detected line
objects_covering: detected lines with >= half their length (and >= 5 px) within 2 px of the truth line
width: median estimate of the covering lines vs truth median width
bands: axis_share_with_a_line_on_it: share of band-axis samples within 0.5 px of a detected line
global: false_length_share: detected length farther than 3 px from every truth line

criteria_note: fixed here, not tuned; used only to label each line as continuous / found_fragmented / missed and each band as protected or not. Joint reading, no single pass/fail for the route.
interpretation: if most line types are continuous on most test tiles and bands are protected: automatic line extraction is feasible at low cost on synthetic data; next step a real sample
if lines are found but fragmented: placement works, joining is the open problem
if a line type is missed (expected risk: pale_1): that type needs its own method
D71 baseline recall shows whether the colour-class failure is removed
stop_rule: one run on test seeds, <= 10 min CPU; no change after the first number
